back: A turbine is turned by water, steam, gas or wind; it drives a generator, in which a coil turning in a magnetic field makes electricity.
Reservoir → intake → penstock → turbine → generator → transformer → grid. Output depends on the head and the volume of water.
Coal burned in a boiler → steam → turbine → generator; steam condensed with cooling water and reused.
Reliable river flow, narrow gorge, hard impermeable rock, storage basin, few people to resettle, access to the grid.
Next to a coalfield (bulky fuel), large cooling-water supply, flat stable land, rail links, away from towns.
Dam completed 1959 on the Zambezi; Kariba South (Zimbabwe) about 1,050 MW after extension; Tonga people resettled; Operation Noah.
Coal-fired station beside the Hwange coalfield; cooling water piped from the Zambezi; two new units added in the early 2020s.
Scrubbers and filters, cleaner renewables, reforestation, rehabilitating mined land and ash dumps, EIA and fair resettlement.
The maximum output of a power station in megawatts (MW); actual output is often lower.
